name: Elisha
description: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy

points: The Lord sent Elijah back to the wilderness of Damascus to anoint Hazael to be king over Syria, Jehu the son of Nimshi to be king over Israel, and Elisha the son of Shaphat of Abel-meholah to be prophet in his room. Him that escaped the sword of Hazael would Jehu slay, and him that escaped Jehu would Elisha slay.

note.label: 1 Kings 19: A Still Small Voice

points: The Most High was telling Elijah not to worry, for he had things set up: Syria would come against the northern kingdom, Jehu would rise up to slay Ahab and all his house, and Elisha would pick up where Elijah left off when it was his time to come home.

note.label: 1 Kings 19: A Still Small Voice

points: Elijah found Elisha plowing with twelve yoke of oxen and cast his mantle, like a cloak, upon him. Elisha left the oxen and ran after Elijah, asking to kiss his father and mother first, then he would follow.

note.label: 1 Kings 19: A Still Small Voice

points: When the Most High is about to take up Elijah into heaven by a whirlwind, Elijah goes with Elisha from Gilgal and tells him to tarry, but Elisha refuses to leave him. At Bethel and at Jericho the sons of the prophets tell Elisha that his master will be taken from him today, and each time he answers that he knows it and bids them hold their peace.

note.label: 2 Kings 2: Elijah Taken Up and a Double Portion for Elisha

points: Elisha sees it and cries, my father, my father, the chariot of Israel and the horsemen thereof, and sees him no more. He takes hold of his own clothes and rends them in two pieces and takes up the mantle of Elijah that fell from him.

note.label: 2 Kings 2: Elijah Taken Up and a Double Portion for Elisha

points: Elisha returns and smites the waters of Jordan with the mantle, asking, where is the Lord God of Elijah, and the waters part so he goes over. The sons of the prophets at Jericho see it and say the spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha, and they bow themselves to the ground before him.

note.label: 2 Kings 2: Elijah Taken Up and a Double Portion for Elisha

points: The waters are healed to this day according to the saying of Elisha. The sign shows that the spirit that was on Elijah now works through Elisha.

note.label: 2 Kings 2: Elijah Taken Up and a Double Portion for Elisha

points: Jehoshaphat asks whether there is not a prophet of the Lord that they may inquire of the Lord by him. One of the king of Israel's servants answers that Elisha the son of Shaphat is there, who poured water on the hands of Elijah.

note.label: 2 Kings 3: Three Kings and the Water in the Ditches

points: Elisha confronts the king of Israel, asking what he has to do with him, and sends him to the prophets of his father and of his mother. The king answers that the Lord has called the three kings together to deliver them into the hand of Moab.

note.label: 2 Kings 3: Three Kings and the Water in the Ditches

points: Elisha says, as the Lord of hosts liveth before whom I stand, that were it not that he regarded the presence of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, he would not look toward the king of Israel nor see him. He addresses the matter only for the sake of the righteous king of Judah.

note.label: 2 Kings 3: Three Kings and the Water in the Ditches

points: A certain woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets cries to Elisha that her husband is dead, that her husband feared the Lord, and that the creditor has come to take her two sons to be bondmen. Because the husband died in debt, the creditor comes to take the sons to work off what is owed.

note.label: 2 Kings 4: The Widow's Oil and the Shunammite's Son

points: Elisha asks what she has in the house, and she says nothing but a pot of oil. He tells her to borrow empty vessels from all her neighbors, not a few, then shut the door upon herself and her sons and pour oil into all the vessels.

note.label: 2 Kings 4: The Widow's Oil and the Shunammite's Son

points: When Elisha comes to the house, the child is dead, laid upon his bed. He goes in, shuts the door upon them both, and prays to the Lord.

note.label: 2 Kings 4: The Widow's Oil and the Shunammite's Son

points: Elisha comes again to Gilgal, where there is a dearth in the land, and the sons of the prophets sit before him. He tells his servant to set on the great pot and seethe pottage for them.

note.label: 2 Kings 4: The Widow's Oil and the Shunammite's Son

points: When Elisha the man of God hears that the king of Israel has rent his clothes, he sends to the king asking why, and says let the man come to him, and he shall know that there is a prophet in Israel.

note.label: 2 Kings 5: Naaman Cleansed and Gehazi Struck

points: Elisha sent word to wash seven times in Jordan. Naaman was wroth because he expected the prophet to come out and wave his hand; he had better rivers at home. That pride almost cost him his healing. When the Lord says do, do; stop wanting God to do it your way.

note.label: Covetous Eyes Will Be Put Out

points: Naaman comes with his horses and chariot and stands at the door of Elisha's house. Elisha sends a messenger out to him, saying go and wash in Jordan seven times, and thy flesh shall come again to thee, and thou shalt be clean.

note.label: 2 Kings 5: Naaman Cleansed and Gehazi Struck

points: Gehazi, the servant of Elisha, reasons that his master has spared Naaman the Syrian by not receiving what he brought, and swears, as the Lord liveth, he will run after him and take somewhat of him. When Naaman sees him running, he lights down from the chariot to meet him and asks whether all is well.

note.label: 2 Kings 5: Naaman Cleansed and Gehazi Struck

points: One servant answers that none of them is, but Elisha the prophet in Israel tells the king of Israel the very words the king of Syria speaks in his bedchamber.

note.label: 2 Kings 6: The Floating Axe Head and the Blinded Host

points: Elisha prays that the Lord open the young man's eyes, and the Lord opens them so he sees the mountain full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha. When Israel goes out to war, there is more with them than with their enemies, for the angels of the Lord are with them.

note.label: 2 Kings 6: The Floating Axe Head and the Blinded Host

points: When the Syrians come down to Elisha, he prays that the Lord smite them with blindness, and the Lord smites them according to the word of Elisha. Elisha tells them this is not the way nor the city, and leads them to Samaria.

note.label: 2 Kings 6: The Floating Axe Head and the Blinded Host

points: In Samaria, Elisha prays that the Lord open their eyes, and they see they are in the midst of the city. The king of Israel asks whether he shall smite them, calling Elisha my father.

note.label: 2 Kings 6: The Floating Axe Head and the Blinded Host

points: Elisha sits in his house with the elders, and the king sends a man before him, but before the messenger arrives Elisha tells the elders to see how this son of a murderer has sent to take away his head, and to shut the door and hold him fast, for the sound of his master's feet is behind him.

note.label: 2 Kings 6: The Floating Axe Head and the Blinded Host

points: Elisha declares the word of the Most High that within a day the famine will break and fine flour and barley will sell cheaply in the gate of Samaria.

note.label: 2 Kings 7: The Word of the Lord in the Gate of Samaria

points: Elisha warns the Shunammite woman whose son he restored to flee the coming seven year famine, and she sojourns in the land of the Philistines.

note.label: 2 Kings 8: The Prophet Weeps Over Israel's Coming Affliction

points: When she returns to appeal to the king for her house and land, Gehazi is at that moment telling the king how Elisha restored a dead body to life.

note.label: 2 Kings 8: The Prophet Weeps Over Israel's Coming Affliction

points: Ben-hadad king of Syria, sick, sends Hazael to inquire of Elisha whether he will recover, for the word of a prophet, also called a seer, was precious in those days.

note.label: 2 Kings 8: The Prophet Weeps Over Israel's Coming Affliction

points: Elisha tells Hazael he will be king over Syria, revealing that leadership can discern spirits at work in a man that the man does not see in himself. Hazael returns and smothers the king with a wet cloth and reigns in his place.

note.label: 2 Kings 8: The Prophet Weeps Over Israel's Coming Affliction

points: Elisha sends one of the children of the prophets to Ramoth-gilead to anoint Jehu king over Israel, pour the oil on his head, and flee.

note.label: 2 Kings 9: Jehu Anointed and the Wicked Kings Cut Off

points: Elisha fell sick of the sickness he would die of, and Joash king of Israel came and wept over him, calling him the chariot of Israel and the horsemen thereof.

note.label: 2 Kings 13: The Death of Elisha and the Arrows of Deliverance

points: Elisha had the king take bow and arrows, laid his own hands on the king's hands, and had him shoot eastward as the arrow of the Lord's deliverance from Syria.

note.label: 2 Kings 13: The Death of Elisha and the Arrows of Deliverance

points: Elisha died and was buried, and when a dead man was cast into his sepulchre and touched his bones, the man revived and stood on his feet.

note.label: 2 Kings 13: The Death of Elisha and the Arrows of Deliverance
